Let \(\alpha=2^{1/16}\) and \(\zeta=\zeta_{16}\). Since
\[
\alpha^8=\sqrt2=\zeta^2+\zeta^{-2}\in \mathbb Q(\zeta),
\]
we have
\[
L=\mathbb Q(\alpha,\zeta),\qquad [L:\mathbb Q]=64.
\]

An automorphism is determined by
\[
\zeta\mapsto \zeta^a,\qquad \alpha\mapsto \zeta^b\alpha,
\]
where \(a\in(\mathbb Z/16\mathbb Z)^\times\), and \(b\) must satisfy the compatibility condition
\[
(-1)^b\sqrt2=\sigma(\sqrt2).
\]
Thus \(b\) is even for \(a\equiv \pm1\pmod 8\), and odd for \(a\equiv \pm3\pmod 8\). Hence
\[
G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)
\]
has order \(64\).

Intermediate fields \(E\) with \([E:\mathbb Q]=8\) correspond to subgroups \(H\le G\) of order \(8\). Also, two such fields are \(\mathbb Q\)-isomorphic iff the corresponding subgroups are conjugate in \(G\): any \(\mathbb Q\)-isomorphism extends to \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), and since \(L\) is the splitting field of \(x^{16}-2\), it stabilizes \(L\).

So we only need the number of conjugacy classes of order-\(8\) subgroups of \(G\).

Let
\[
N=\{(2j,1):j\in\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z\}\cong C_8
\]
be the subgroup fixing \(\mathbb Q(\zeta)\). For an order-\(8\) subgroup \(H\), put \(M=H\cap N\) and let \(B\) be its image in
\[
G/N\cong (\mathbb Z/16\mathbb Z)^\times.
\]
Then \(|M||B|=8\). A direct subgroup count gives:

- \(|M|=8\): one class, namely \(H=N\).
- \(|M|=4\): four classes, according to the order-\(2\) image \(B=\langle 7\rangle,\langle 15\rangle,\langle 9\rangle\), with two distinct lift classes for \(\langle 9\rangle\).
- \(|M|=2\): two classes, one with image \(\{1,7,9,15\}\), and one with image \(\langle 3\rangle=\{1,3,9,11\}\).
- \(|M|=1\): no class, because there is no complement mapping isomorphically onto all of \((\mathbb Z/16\mathbb Z)^\times\).

Therefore the number of conjugacy classes of order-\(8\) subgroups is
\[
1+4+2=7.
\]

So the number of distinct \(\mathbb Q\)-isomorphism classes is

\[
\boxed{7}.
\]
